transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Patel, it is good to see you. I want to talk to you about how the surgery went yesterday and a mistake that happened during the procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? The surgeon told me before I went under that everything was routine and there were no risks to worry about.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize. I am the one responsible for that part of the operation, and I made an error. I placed a small metal clip on the wrong structure. In a laparoscopic surgery, we use these clips to seal off blood vessels or ducts. I put one where it didn't belong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You put a clip in the wrong place. Why is that even possible?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a technical error on my part. Once I realized it, I immediately corrected it and removed the clip, but that required me to perform an additional procedure to make sure there was no damage. Does that make sense so far, or can I clarify any of those terms?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand the words you're using, but I don't understand how you "just" do that. My last doctor told me the same thing about a "routine" test and then I spent three weeks in the ER because they missed a bleed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry for that mistake and for the fact that the information you were given earlier was contradictory. I take full responsibility for the error in the OR.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly why I don't trust any of you. You say it's routine, then you're cutting things you aren't supposed to, and then you just tell me after the fact. I feel like I'm just another chart to you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling frustrated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrated isn't the word. I feel like I'm being lied to by a system that—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go in a few minutes to check on another patient, so let's focus on the clinical part. Does that make sense? Did you have any other questions about the clip itself?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the clip. I care about why I was told one thing by the surgeon and another by you. Who is actually in charge here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, I am the one who performed the clip placement and I am the one who made the mistake. It was my error, not the surgeon's. To make sure we are on the same page, do you understand why the extra procedure was necessary because of that clip?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I get it. You messed up and had to fix it. Great. Now what? Am I just supposed to go home and hope nothing falls off inside me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep a close eye on your recovery. One thing we can do is schedule a follow-up ultrasound for next Tuesday to confirm everything is healing correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tuesday. And who is doing that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: My team will handle the imaging. You just need to make sure you fast for six hours before that appointment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens if the ultrasound shows another mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will review the results together on Wednesday morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want this in writing. I want a full report of the error and the correction before I leave this room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can have a summary typed up for you by tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow? I'm leaving today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't get the formal report signed off that quickly, but I'll make sure it's sent to your portal by noon tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Whatever. I've heard "tomorrow" from this hospital before.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'll make sure it happens. We'll see you on Tuesday for the scan.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have to go in a few minutes') and interrupts the patient's emotional expression of being lied to by the system.

E.justification: Error (wrong clip placement) named in second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense so far', 'do you understand why').

A.justification: Direct apologies used ('I apologize', 'I am very sorry'), takes full personal responsibility, and maintains it despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Resident names one emotion ('frustrated') but then immediately redirects to clinical facts, and uses generic validation ('I understand') later.

T.justification: Specific next step (ultrasound) with timeline (Tuesday) and patient role (fast for six hours) is provided.
